title: God curse the snake to crawl to the ground, does that mean that the snake have feet before?
paragraphs: God curse the snake to crawl to the ground, does that mean that the snake have feet before?
That question cuts deeper than it looks.

Because in Genesis 3:14, God says to the serpent:
“On your belly you shall go…”
Which raises the tension:
Was the serpent already crawling… or was this a downgrade?
Let’s walk it carefully.
The Text Doesn’t Explicitly Say It Had Legs

Scripture never directly says: “the serpent had feet before.”
So we shouldn’t claim more than what’s written.
But it does strongly imply a change in status.
Why?
Because God calls it a curse.

And a curse always means:
loss, humiliation, or degradation.
“On Your Belly” = Humiliation Language
In the ancient world, crawling on your belly symbolized defeat and shame.
You see echoes of this in other Scriptures:

Enemies “lick the dust”
Kings fall face down in defeat
So this isn’t just about biology…
It’s about position.
The serpent is being brought low.
So Did It Have Legs Before?
There are two main faithful interpretations:
1. Literal Change View

The serpent may have had some form of mobility (possibly limbs)
God physically altered it as part of the curse
2. Symbolic/Humiliation View

The focus is not anatomy
It’s about being cast down, disgraced, and defeated
Both agree on one thing:
👉 The serpent went from elevated to humiliated.
But Don’t Miss the Bigger War
Right after the curse, God says this:

“I will put enmity between you and the woman…
He shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise His heel.” (Genesis 3:15)
This is massive.
This is the first whisper of the Gospel.
The serpent isn’t just an animal.
It’s tied to Satan—the deceiver.
And God is declaring:

👉 “You may strike…
but you will be crushed.”
Fulfilled in Jesus
That crushing happens at the cross.
Through Jesus Christ:

Sin is paid for
Satan is defeated
Death loses its grip
The serpent’s curse points forward to a cosmic victory.
Here’s Where It Hits You
This isn’t just about a snake.
It’s about rebellion → consequence → redemption.

The same voice that deceived Eve
is still whispering today:
“Did God really say…?”

And every time we believe the lie,
we repeat the fall.
But here’s the hope:

👉 The same God who cursed the serpent
also made a way to rescue you.

The Gospel, Clear and Unfiltered
You have sinned (Romans 3:23)
Sin separates you from God
You cannot fix it yourself
Jesus lived perfectly, died in your place, and rose again
If you repent and trust Him, you are forgiven and made new
Reflection
Where have you been believing the serpent’s voice instead of God’s truth?
“Jesus crushed the lie.”
Send this to someone who’s been questioning Genesis or struggling with doubt.
You’ll want this when questions about the Bible come back.

This isn’t just about what the serpent lost…
It’s about what Jesus restored.
This isn’t the end of your story.
